newsitem.title: CYPRUS: British woman set to testify in Cyprus AIDS trial.
newsitem.headline: British woman set to testify in Cyprus AIDS trial.

text.p: A British woman is set to testify against her former Cypriot lover in a Cyprus court on Thursday for giving her the deadly AIDS virus.

The case, brought by 45-year-old Janette Pink against former boyfriend Pavlos Georgiou, 39, is the first test in court here on how to handle allegations that an HIV carrier recklessly or deliberately transmitted the deadly virus.
Pink, who arrived on the island at the weekend for the hearing which is expected to last around 10 days, had a two-hour meeting on Wednesday with government prosecuters.

The 45-year-old mother of two, who moved to Cyprus in 1993 but went back to Britain last year when she discovered she had Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome, declined to comment to waiting reporters.

Cypriot authorities are charging Georgiou, who is HIV positive and has four children, for contravening a decades-old law banning the transmission of contagious diseases either unlawfully or negligently.
He has denied the charge, which carries a prison sentence of up to two years in jail, a 1,500 pound fine, or both.

Pink, from Basildon, Essex, has accused Georgiou of keeping her in the dark about his condition during their three-year affair, and lying to her about the death of his wife. She also suffered from AIDS.
